citations.quote: control is transferred according to the rules for the specific exception condition and the rules for the USE statement following the execution of the associated declarative procedure
control is transferred according to the rules in 9.1.12, Input-output exception processing
No such procedure is executed if one of the conditions specified in 9.1.12.1, Successful completion, occurs
The exception-name for successful completion with an I-O status value that is not '00' is EC-I-O-WARNING

cases.reason: The general format is the same in both editions. The words differ in b): 2002 states the USE-procedure transfer itself, while 2023 defers to its new 9.1.12 'Input-output exception processing' (which adds exception-checking PERFORM ... WHEN). The difference a program can show is in which READs reach c): in 2002 only an unsuccessful completion carries an exception, so a successful READ with status 02 or 04 runs NOT AT END and no declarative even with EC-ALL checking on. In 2023, 9.1.13.1 gives those statuses EC-I-O-WARNING, which is an exception other than at end, so they fall under b). The pointer's evidence (pb338) shows only a). Probes p05 and p07 show b)1, b)2, c) and the 02/04 case correct at --std 2002.
cases.needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 the compiler runs the USE procedure on 51 and goes to the end of the READ, skips NOT AT END on 51 with or without USE, honours GO TO in NOT AT END, and treats 02/04 as successful with no declarative (probes p05, p07); a 2002 witness from them

cases.reason: The reader treated 2023's a)/b) restructuring as a widening. It is also a NARROWING. In 2002 the governing first sentence applies to EVERY declarative that executes RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT: control goes to the implicit CONTINUE after 'the statement that was executing when control was transferred to the declarative'; the 'When an exception condition caused...' sentence only refines which statement that is for exceptions. 2023 GR2 defines the target only in two cases: a) an exception caused the procedure, b) a PERFORM in the nondeclarative portion executed it. A USE BEFORE REPORTING declarative is neither: it is 'implicitly performed' by the report writer during GENERATE/INITIATE/TERMINATE, and RESUME is legal there in both editions (SR1: only in a declarative). So 2002 GR2 prescribes control after the GENERATE statement; 2023 GR2 is silent, and the 2023 row's evidence (pb892, pb141, pb1432, all exception or PERFORM cases) says nothing about it. Probe r01: RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT in USE BEFORE REPORTING DET-A compiles and runs at 2002 and 2023 identically: the declarative exits (no DECL-END), AFTER-G2 shows, but the detail line AMT=02 is still printed and LINE-COUNTER ends at 03, i.e. the compiler returns into the GENERATE rather than transferring to its end. Under the 2002 text that is probably wrong (the remainder of the GENERATE should not run; LC 02, no AMT=02 line), subject to the 'unless general rules associated with the applicable statement specify otherwise' escape, which the GENERATE and USE BEFORE REPORTING rules do not use.
